model.title: Protecting Investors’ Personally Identifiable Information Act

summary.lead: Official summary (Congressional Research Service, Introduced in House):

blocks.text: Protecting Investors' Personally Identifiable Information Act
This bill limits certain disclosures of personally identifiable information belonging to a participant in the securities market for purposes of tracking market activity.

Specifically, the bill prohibits the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) from requiring a national securities exchange, a national securities association, or a member of such an exchange or association to provide such information to satisfy the reporting requirements of the Consolidated Audit Trail (data used by regulators to track market activity).

This bill limits how personal information about people in the securities market can be collected for tracking market activity. Specifically, it bars the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) from requiring a national securities exchange, a national securities association, or a member of either of these to hand over such information to meet the reporting rules of the Consolidated Audit Trail, which is the data regulators use to track market activity.
